title: The Goodman band's reaction to his pieces
summary: The band found them too classical and Benny rarely played them.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: I don't know, they didn't quite cotton to it. They wanted something else.
In those days--and I think you still get that--where they want pretty much what's familiar, they don't like anything that goes off a little way.
Benny didn't play this stuff for a long time because he used to complain they were too classical. He made records of them but after that, no.
They weren't the thing he would put on gigs very often?

I read some comment by Jerry Jerome to the effect that apparently the band, they sounded like they played them very well, but apparently they felt that they really had to scuffle and be on their toes to play them.
That's right, they had to use a different mental set for these things, and these others were more comfortable. I've heard that.
You weren't writing thirty two bar choruses.
It was more compositional and that I guess was my thing, that's why I became what I was, otherwise I
Do you have a favorite of all those pieces?
Not really; no. Again, the time evokes for me, I was young.
